answer: In a garden marketplace where AI agents trade yarrow seeds and sable-colored pots, each seller identity must lock $100 in escrow for 30 days before receiving one order slot. Creating accounts is cheap, but capacity is tied to locked capital, not account count. An attacker seeking 1,000 seller slots must immobilize $100,000 for a month, paying financing costs even if no fraud is detected; splitting the same funds across more names adds no capacity.
